name: Trainer Intelligence Hypothesis A - handicap positioning rating drop
description: Tests whether horses returning off a rating at least 5lb below their career-best mark, with a real previous win somewhere in their history, outperform the market's own de-vigged implied probability -- the brief's Section 12A handicap-positioning hypothesis. Backtested over the FULL historical bootstrap (2023-01-01 to present, 313,182 rated runs with a real prior run, 45,396 distinct horse names, matched by name to sidestep the known horse.id dedup bug).
rule_definition: QUALIFYING: rating_drop (prior_max_official_rating - current_official_rating) >= 5.0 AND has_previous_win == true. CONTROL: everyone else with a known outcome and a de-vig-able race (>=2 runners with a real starting_price). Compared via actual_wins vs sum-of-market-probability expected_wins for each group separately.

historical_evidence.conclusion: NEGATIVE RESULT (initial cut): the qualifying group tracks the market's own expectation MORE closely (-4.6% relative shortfall) than the control group does (-12.5% relative shortfall) -- i.e. no edge over the market was found for this specific rule at this threshold. Statistical caveat: pooled at runner level, not race-level resampled (brief Section 24) -- read as descriptive/suggestive, not a validated test. Worth noting both groups show the market itself slightly overpredicting relative to realised outcomes across this whole population, a separate observation from the hypothesis itself.
historical_evidence.statistical_caveat: Pooled at runner level, NOT race-level resampled -- observations within the same race are not independent.

prospective_results.note: already backtested against the full historical population in historical_evidence; no separate prospective run needed unless the rule is revised
